Date: 2028-11-16T15:02:00Z
Subject: Mutual action plan + proposed owner for implementation

Hi Jamie / Ethan — great conversation today. Thanks for walking through Clairmont's two initial use cases (Inpatient summary and discharge note augmentation). Per our discovery notes:

- Priority 1: Inpatient summary pipeline, target throughput ~150 reqs/min, 95th pct latency goal < 450ms
- Priority 2: Discharge augmentation (batch processing of 2k records/day)
- Data: PHI will be present; customer requires private deployment (VPC) and SOC2 evidence
- Desired go-live window: mid-February 2029 (customer requested)

Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones. The commercial terms are signed pending SOW finalization — procurement looped in on next steps.

Olga — can you take point on onboarding/implementation and map CS owners? Monica should be primary PM for the onboarding sprints; Karthik can support for technical discovery and model onboarding constraints.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Internal-Sales→CS warm handoff call (30–45m) the week of 11/27 to align on scope and constraints
2) CS to produce a 30/60/90 onboarding plan and a short risk register for infra/PHI handling
3) Deliverable: updated MAP + SOW v3 with explicit VPC/KMS clauses (Monica / Olga)

Attachments: Clairmont_MutualActionPlan_v2.xlsx (draft)

Ben
Senior Account Executive

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-11-19T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + proposed owner for implementation

Thanks, all — happy to take PM lead. Quick notes from a CS implementation POV after reading the MAP:

Open questions / risks:
- Security: Clairmont requires KMS integration and audit logs retained for 7 years — we need Legal to confirm the retention SLA and Ops on exportability
- SSO: Do they require SCIM provisioning and IdP metadata? If yes, we need their Okta/IdP test tenant before sprint 1
- Data ingress: For discharge batch ingestion, will they push to an S3 bucket or will Redwood pull? Need to confirm transfer pattern and encryption-at-rest keys

Proposed milestone owners (first pass):
- Sprint 0 (environment & access): Monica (PM) + Karthik (tech) — deliverable: deployment runbook and network diagram
- Sprint 1 (model onboarding & prefix caching): Karthik — deliverable: validated model variant and sequence length perf notes
- Sprint 2 (end-to-end test & UAT): Monica — deliverable: UAT checklist and acceptance criteria

I'll annotate the MAP with these owners and estimated days (sprint 0 = 7 days, sprint 1 = 10 days, sprint 2 = 5 days). Also attaching an updated SOW draft with a placeholder for the VPC/KMS language (SOW_draft_Clairmont_v3.pdf) — legal will need to finalize.

I have one operational ask for Clairmont: can you confirm whether PHI transfer will occur within their own VPC peering or via a secure SFTP endpoint? That will affect scheduling for networking and firewall rules.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Rodriguez <jamie@clairmont.health>

Thanks, everyone — this looks good. A few quick replies from Clairmont: 

- Preferred go-live: target week of 2029-02-12 (internal board aligned on that window)
- Procurement contact: procurement@clairmont.health (copied here) — they will want SOW and final pricing; procurement also asked whether there is a standard Data Processing Addendum we can sign
- PHI transfer: we prefer VPC peering for production and an S3-based batch drop (encrypted) for the discharge pipeline during early testing. We can provide an Okta test tenant for SSO work next week.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood will provide a UAT environment that mirrors production sequence-length limits? We need to run a subset of records for acceptance testing.

Jamie Rodriguez
Head of Technology Operations
